title: Gastrulation in one picture

objective.text: Explain how the two-layered disc becomes three germ layers in week 3.

body.general: How does a flat disc of two cell layers become three? In week 3 the disc turns into three layers, called germ layers; this process is gastrulation [f1]. It starts when a groove, the primitive streak, appears on the top layer, the epiblast [f2]. Epiblast cells crowd into the groove and slip underneath [f3]. The first ones push out the bottom layer, the hypoblast, and become endoderm [f4]. Later ones fill the middle as mesoderm [f5]. Cells left on top become ectoderm [f6]. So all three layers come from the epiblast [f7].
body.mbbs: Gastrulation is the week-3 process that turns the bilaminar disc into three germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm [f1]. It begins when the primitive streak appears on the epiblast, around days 14–15 (CS6) [f2]. Epiblast cells migrate to the streak, lose their links to neighbours and slip beneath it (invagination) [f3]. The first cells through displace the hypoblast and form definitive endoderm [f4]. Later cells spread between epiblast and endoderm as intraembryonic mesoderm [f5]. Cells that stay in the epiblast become ectoderm [f6]. So all three germ layers, and every tissue they build, come from the epiblast [f7].

facts.text: Gastrulation is the week-3 process that forms the three germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.
facts.note: R05b: human gastrula at CS7, 16–19 d

facts.text: It starts when the primitive streak appears on the epiblast, around days 14–15 (Carnegie stage 6).
facts.note: R06 has the streak at ~13 d post-ovulation, within the ±1–2 d spread (dossier §1)

facts.text: Epiblast cells move toward the streak, let go of their neighbours and slip underneath; this inward move is invagination.
The first cells to move in push into the hypoblast and replace it, forming the embryo's endoderm.
Later cells settle between the epiblast and the new endoderm as mesoderm.
Cells that stay in the epiblast become ectoderm.
So all three germ layers come from the epiblast, and together they build every tissue of the embryo.
Gastrulation opens the period most sensitive to teratogens, weeks 3 to 8.
Beyond Langman: human single-cell and spatial studies of CS7 embryos find epiblast, streak, new mesoderm, endoderm and primordial germ cells side by side.
Beyond Langman (mouse study): a few cells of the old lower layer mix into the new gut endoderm rather than all being pushed aside.

misconceptions.right: Epiblast cells move in and replace the hypoblast; they form the endoderm.

misconceptions.wrong: The three layers come from different starting layers.
misconceptions.right: All three come from the epiblast.

misconceptions.wrong: Epiblast and ectoderm are the same thing.
misconceptions.right: The epiblast is the upper layer of the two-layered disc; ectoderm is only the part of it left behind after cells move in.

checks.prompt: All three germ layers come from which layer?
checks.why: All three layers come from the epiblast: some cells move in, and those left on top become ectoderm.

checks.prompt: What happens to the hypoblast during gastrulation?
options: Epiblast cells replace it as endoderm
checks.why: Epiblast cells push the hypoblast aside and take its place as endoderm; the hypoblast does not turn into it.

checks.prompt: Put the steps of gastrulation in order.
options: The primitive streak appears on the epiblast
Epiblast cells move in through the streak
Cells replace the hypoblast as endoderm
Cells spread between the layers as mesoderm
checks.why: Cells go in through the streak; the first ones make endoderm, and the ones after them make mesoderm.

adult: These three layers go on to build every tissue of the body [f7].

remember.a: Three germ layers, ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm, in week 3 [f1].

remember.q: Which layer do all three germ layers come from?

remember.a: The first epiblast cells through the streak push it aside and form endoderm [f4].
